### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **6** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, `@objectstack/service-automation`, `@objectstack/service-cache`, `@objectstack/service-cluster-redis`, `@objectstack/service-cluster`, `@objectstack/service-sms`, touching **36** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **7** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/vitest.config.ts`, `packages/services/service-automation/vitest.config.ts`, `packages/services/service-cache/README.md`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**7** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/deployment/production-readiness.mdx`  _(via MetricsRegistry (symbol, a top-level type))_
- `content/docs/kernel/contracts/cache-service.mdx`  _(via CacheServicePlugin (symbol, a top-level class), RedisCacheAdapter (symbol, a top-level class), keyPrefix (symbol, a field of class RedisCacheAdapter; a field of interface CacheServicePluginRedisOptions; a field of interface ClusterDriverConnection; a field of type CacheAdapterPlan))_
- `content/docs/kernel/services.mdx`  _(via CacheServicePlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/plugins/anatomy.mdx`  _(via optionalDependencies (symbol, a field of class CacheServicePlugin))_
- `content/docs/plugins/packages.mdx`  _(via RedisCacheAdapter (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/lifecycle.mdx`  _(via optionalDependencies (symbol, a field of class CacheServicePlugin))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/plugin-spec.mdx`  _(via optionalDependencies (symbol, a field of class CacheServicePlugin))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v16.mdx`  _(via keyPrefix (symbol, a field of class RedisCacheAdapter; a field of interface CacheServicePluginRedisOptions; a field of interface ClusterDriverConnection; a field of type CacheAdapterPlan))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-5.mdx`  _(via keyPrefix (symbol, a field of class RedisCacheAdapter; a field of interface CacheServicePluginRedisOptions; a field of interface ClusterDriverConnection; a field of type CacheAdapterPlan))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **7** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/vitest.config.ts`, `packages/services/service-automation/vitest.config.ts`, `packages/services/service-cache/README.md`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **26** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **64** of **227** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **163** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **163**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **104** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **30** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 58ab03dea13e805214effb0bae72571ab066c2e9` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `9722a102df5d155462a3091a7bb798116f07cf0e` — the merge of head `820d1fb9fb69e2f0b0efe77266524c5e9c88e726` into base `58ab03dea13e805214effb0bae72571ab066c2e9`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 9722a102df5d155462a3091a7bb798116f07cf0e && git checkout 9722a102df5d155462a3091a7bb798116f07cf0e
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 58ab03dea13e805214effb0bae72571ab066c2e9 820d1fb9fb69e2f0b0efe77266524c5e9c88e726 && git checkout -B drift-repro 58ab03dea13e805214effb0bae72571ab066c2e9 && git merge --no-ff 820d1fb9fb69e2f0b0efe77266524c5e9c88e726

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 58ab03dea13e805214effb0bae72571ab066c2e9
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 58ab03dea13e805214effb0bae72571ab066c2e9` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

The four prose-face files (`.changeset/31553-shared-redis-cache-adapter.md`, `content/docs/kernel/cluster.mdx`, `content/docs/kernel/contracts/cache-service.mdx`, `content/docs/plugins/packages.mdx`) were read for agreement with the code, never reviewed: their sentence check is the lane seat's ACCEPT.

Code outside the diff was read in the live tree, never reviewed: the files after the `+` above, plus the published sources the request path runs on, `better-auth@1.7.12` `dist/api/rate-limiter/index.mjs` and `dist/api/index.mjs`, and `ioredis@6.0.0` `built/Redis.js` and `built/redis/RedisOptions.js` (read from the registry tarballs; nothing was built or run). Also read: `scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs` (the disposition categories and the prescription refusal), AGENTS.md Post-Task step 3, ADR-0069 D2, the ADR-0087 addendum, and the cloud control plane's `packages/service-cloud/src/control-plane-preset.ts`.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Published spec: untouched.** No path under `packages/spec`. `ICacheService` (`get`/`set`/`delete`/`has`/`clear`/`stats`, `ttl` in seconds) and `IClusterService` (`driver: string` is already a member, line 267 of `cluster-service.ts`) are the contracts the diff implements against; neither gains or loses a member. Right.
2. **`@objectstack/service-cache` public surface widens and narrows.** Widens: `RedisCacheAdapter` is implemented (it was a class whose every method threw); new option `redis: CacheServicePluginRedisOptions` (`client`, `keyPrefix`, `defaultTtl`); new exported types `CacheServicePluginRedisOptions`, `RedisCacheClient`; new exported pure function `planCacheAdapter` with its `CacheAdapterPlan` / `CacheAdapterPlanInput` types; `adapter: 'redis'` now boots where it threw. `redisUrl` and `RedisCacheAdapterOptions.url` are deprecated (never read before, never read now); `RedisCacheAdapter` without a `client` throws a `TypeError` naming the fix (before: constructed, then every method threw). The plugin gains `optionalDependencies: ['com.objectstack.service.cluster']`. Narrows: `CacheServicePlugin({ adapter: 'memory' })` throws at `init` when `declaresMultiNode(process.env)` is true AND the registered `cluster` service's `driver` is `redis` — one configuration that used to boot. The declaration names exactly this. Right.
3. **`@objectstack/service-cluster` widens by two value exports and one type:** `offerClusterDriverConnection`, `readClusterDriverConnection`, `ClusterDriverConnection`. The offer is a non-enumerable, non-writable, non-configurable own property on the cluster instance under `Symbol.for('@objectstack/service-cluster:driver-connection')`, holding a frozen copy of `{ driver, client, keyPrefix }`; a second offer on the same instance throws; the reader answers `undefined` for a non-object, an absent offer, a malformed offer or another driver, and never throws. Nothing is added to the spec contract. Right.
4. **`@objectstack/service-cluster-redis`:** one call in `redisDriverFactory`, offering `{ driver: 'redis', client, keyPrefix }` on the facade it already returns, before its `close` wrapper. Its own commands, keys and `close()` are unchanged. Right.
5. **Dependency graph:** `@objectstack/service-cache` takes `@objectstack/service-cluster` at runtime (for `declaresMultiNode` and the reader); `service-cluster`'s own runtime deps are `core` and `spec` only, so no cycle; `service-cluster-redis` and `ioredis-mock` are dev-only in `service-cache`, `plugin-auth`, `service-sms`, `service-automation`. `pnpm-lock.yaml` moves workspace links and the already-present `ioredis-mock@8.13.1` resolution only. `Validate Package Dependencies` is `success` on this head. Right.
6. **Wire, storage, metadata protocol: nothing.** No route, no table, no object, no authorable key. The Redis keys this adds live under the deployment's existing cluster prefix at `keyPrefix + "cache:" + key` (default `os:cache:`). `Metadata-protocol: none` is right.
7. **Consumers of the `cache` slot needed no change:** better-auth's counters (`createLazyCacheRateLimitStorage` → `incrementFixedWindow` → `store.get`/`store.set` with a JSON string and a TTL in seconds), the inbound token bucket (`SharedTokenBucketLimiter.consumeOnce`, same shape), the OTP budget, the SMS day quota and the `notify` per-address limit (both through `createLazyCounterStore`). Each already stores a JSON string and accepts a string back (`parseCounter`, `parseBucket`), which is what the Redis adapter hands back. Right.

### ② Semver level

Changeset `.changeset/31553-shared-redis-cache-adapter.md`: `@objectstack/service-cache`, `@objectstack/service-cluster`, `@objectstack/service-cluster-redis` at **patch**, the three packages whose published source moves; `plugin-auth`, `service-sms`, `service-automation` move `devDependencies`, `vitest.config.ts` and tests only, so they owe none (`Check Changeset` is `success`). Both declaration lines are line-initial on the PR body and the changeset body: `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: none`. AGENTS.md Post-Task step 3: the arm pair is closed (`(widening)`/`(narrowing)`), `(narrowing)` is BREAKING, and "a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch` and keeps its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition"; `check-changeset-no-major` refuses `major` repo-wide. The changeset summary carries the `!` (`feat(service-cache)!:`), the body carries `**BREAKING**` for the one configuration, and exactly one disposition marker: `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)` with a why. **(e) holds**, on all four counts:

- *Declaration.* `yes (narrowing)` is well-formed (one arm from the closed pair), and `reviewFace` reads a `narrowing` arm on a `yes` as the narrowing face (its header says so: "`yes (narrowing)` included: a diff that widens and narrows owes the narrowing face"). The widening (judgments 2–3) and the narrowing (judgment 2) are both real, so `yes (narrowing)` is the exact declaration; `no (narrowing)` would deny the widening.
- *BREAKING banner.* Present, scoped to the configuration actually refused, with Before / Now / remedy. Matches `planCacheAdapter`.
- *ADR-0087 marker.* Honest, not only green. The ledger serves `objectstack migrate meta`; nothing at rest records the adapter choice, no schema key, stored row, authorable key or exported type is removed or renamed, so there is no entry to write (`registered` would be false data). The remedy sentence ("drop `adapter`, or pass `adapter: 'redis'`") is the one-line fix step 3 asks of a breaking changeset, not a FROM-to-TO rewrite in arrow or table form, so the category's own refusal (a body carrying a migration prescription) does not apply. `runtime-interface-only` / `type-surface-only` / `runtime-export-retired` need a retired or narrowed symbol to name, and none exists. The gate ran on this head in the `Check Changeset` job (`pr-automation.yml`, "Require an ADR-0087 disposition on a declared-breaking changeset"): `success`.
- *Patch grade.* Right by the rule quoted above; `Metadata-protocol: none` because nothing an author writes changes.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Card Do 2 vs Do 3, and the claim line.** The card says "`adapter: 'memory'` stays the default and its branch is not touched" (Do 2) and "multi-replica declared and no shared cache registered ⇒ refuse boot loudly" (Do 3). The PR resolves the overlap in favour of Do 3 for the one case where both apply (explicit `memory` under declared multi-node on the redis driver), and declares it as the narrowing. The card's claim comment 6722766461 still reads `Clause-②: no`; the os-dev-report records the PM thread's ruling that `yes (narrowing)` supersedes it. Stale, not false in effect — nit N2.
- **Refusal scope = the redis driver only, as ordered.** Multi-node declared over the memory driver (reachable only past `OS_ALLOW_MEMORY_CLUSTER_MULTINODE=true`) or with no cluster service stays memory, as today, plus one new `warn`; that is the behaviour the review order names for (a), narrower than Do 3's literal. A driver named `redis` that offers no connection is refused (the dev's open question 1, recommendation A): under R2 that deployment plainly intends a shared store, and with the workspace's fixed versioning it is reachable only through a third-party driver. Accepted; the warn (open question 2, recommendation A) is additive logging, not a resolution change.
- **Redis outage on the request paths — bounded, but the bound is the driver's.** `onRequestRateLimit` in `better-auth@1.7.12` does `await storage.consume(key, rule)` with no catch and `onRequest` awaits it with no catch, so a thrown Redis error fails the auth request (the PR says so; the status code is NOT MEASURED, as the PR says). The inbound middleware catches and lets the request through. The derived connection is `base.duplicate()`, which in ioredis 6 is `new Redis({ ...this.options })`, so it inherits the driver factory's `lazyConnect: true`, `maxRetriesPerRequest: 3` and `enableAutoPipelining: true`, and ioredis's defaults `connectTimeout: 10000` and no `commandTimeout`. A refused connection fails a command in well under a second; a black-holed host can hold one for about three connect attempts of 10 s each before the error surfaces. Finite on every path, so (d)'s "nothing unbounded" holds; the length is the cluster driver's own posture for its locks and KV, inherited by design. Nit N1, with a candidate card.
- **No `error` listener on the derived client.** ioredis logs `[ioredis] Unhandled error event` to `console.error` when a connection error has no listener; it does not throw. The driver's base client has none either. Part of N1.
- **Two-process leg is NOT MEASURED in CI** (skipped when `redis-server` is not on PATH; ran locally on 7.0.15 per the PR). The in-process leg (two kernels over `ioredis-mock`) runs everywhere. Accepted; a real-Redis CI leg would cost minutes the CI budget rule guards, so it is a card for the PM thread to weigh, not a condition here.
- **Who mounts the plugin without options.** The cloud control plane does (`control-plane-preset.ts`: `new CacheServicePlugin()`), so a cloud deployment that declares multi-node over the redis driver moves its control-plane cache to Redis with it; today the control plane is a singleton and declares nothing, so nothing changes there. The CLI's `src` names `@objectstack/service-cache` only in tests (the dependency is in `packages/cli/package.json`), so how `os serve` mounts it was not read here; the PR's statement that it mounts the plugin with no options is taken from the PR and `docs/HARDENING.md`, not verified in this record.
- **Dependency direction.** `service-cache` → `service-cluster` is new; it is the same direction cloud-connection took in #31584 and introduces no cycle (judgment 5). Accepted.
- **Author:** `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; no login note owed.
- **Check-runs on `820d1fb9` at review time (about 17:30Z):** Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards, Check Changeset, Check PR Size, Spec property liveness, Validate Package Dependencies, Check Documentation Links, Flag docs affected, Lint · ESLint, Lint · docs & code guards, Lint · CI release & engine gates, the three Lint · scoped lanes, Lint · tooling self-tests, Type Check · source gates, Type Check · debt ledger, Plan Test Core shards, Test Core (5/8), Build UI Deps, Live E2E UI, Dogfood Regression Gate all `success`; Build Core, Test Core 1–4 and 6–8, Test UI 1–16, Build Docs, Build & E2E UI, Lint UI, Type Check UI, Type Check · workspace, Type Check · consumer gates, Lint · PM dispatch-gates and Lint · repo & tooling gates still `in_progress`. The queue reads their conclusions at enqueue; none is in this record.

### ④ Design judgment

**The narrowing itself, against the published surface on `main`.** On `main`, `CacheServicePlugin({ adapter: 'memory' })` registers a `MemoryCacheAdapter` on every node and `RedisCacheAdapter` is unusable, so a declared multi-node deployment on the redis driver could only ever run per-process counters, with nothing at boot saying so — the hole ADR-0069 D2 names ("use a shared store (not in-memory) for multi-node"). The narrowing takes away exactly the ability to boot that deployment with a knowingly per-process cache, and only there: single node keeps `memory` explicit or implicit, the memory driver and the absent cluster keep memory, and the error names its remedy. It makes the card's Do 3 real in the one topology R3 scopes the card to. Holds.

**(a) R3 — single node and every non-redis driver resolve as today.** `planCacheAdapter` returns `{ kind: 'memory' }` before `input.cluster()` is ever called when `multiNode` is false (the `requested === 'redis'` arm is the only earlier branch, and it was a throw on `main`); `init` then runs the same `new MemoryCacheAdapter({ ...this.options.memory, metrics })`, the same `registerService('cache', …)` and the same info line as `main`, with no `warn`. The predicate is `declaresMultiNode()` from `split-brain-guard.ts` — the same function and the same `process.env` the split-brain guard, cloud#3880 and #31584's ledger read, so the four cannot drift. The driver name is `IClusterService.driver`, the string `defineCluster` parsed and `ComposedClusterService` carries. Multi-node over a non-redis driver or with no cluster: memory plus one `warn` naming the cost. Pinned: the context-double case with the info line verbatim and `reads` not containing `cluster`; the real-kernel single-node case over the redis driver; the decision table's memory-driver and no-cluster rows. Holds.

**The refusal.** Fires only when `multiNode` is true AND `describeDriver(cluster) === 'redis'` AND (`requested === 'memory'`, or no `redis.client` and `readClusterDriverConnection(cluster, 'redis')` is `undefined`). It throws from `init` before anything registers, the split-brain guard's posture, and each message names the fix. `adapter: 'redis'` with no connection anywhere also refuses (that path threw on `main` too). Pinned in the decision table, the context double and a real-kernel boot. Holds.

**(b) The seam stays framework-internal.** `packages/spec` is untouched; `IClusterService` gains no member; the offer is two functions in `service-cluster` and one call in the redis driver. The design arguments the order asked to see hold in code: non-enumerable (`Object.keys`, spread, `JSON.stringify` of the facade never show a live client — pinned), written once (second offer throws — pinned), `Symbol.for` so the ESM and CJS copies of `service-cluster` resolve one key (pinned by spelling). The reader validates shape (`driver` and `keyPrefix` strings) and never throws. Ordering: `ClusterServicePlugin.init` builds the facade through `defineCluster`, which calls the factory that offers, then `registerService('cluster', facade)`; `optionalDependencies` hoists that `init` ahead of the cache's (ADR-0116 order-if-present), and the kernel runs every `init` before any `start`, so the cache reads a facade that already offers — pinned by the real-kernel boot with the cache plugin `use`d first. When no cluster plugin is composed, `ctx.getService('cluster')` throws `[Kernel] Service 'cluster' not found`, caught into `undefined`; the kernel logs nothing for that miss. Holds.

**(c) `rateLimit.customStorage`, never `secondaryStorage`.** `plugin-auth`'s production source is untouched (the diff there is `package.json` devDependencies, `vitest.config.ts`, one test and one fixture). `auth-manager-auth-instance.ts` still wires `customStorage: this.config.rateLimitStorage` and sets `secondaryStorage` only when the host supplies one. The three new two-replica tests count through `createLazyCacheRateLimitStorage` with `resolveCache` resolving `resolveKernelCache(ctx)` (the seam `AuthPlugin` hands better-auth) and through `createLazyCounterStore` (SMS, notify). The adapter is reached only as the `cache` service. Sessions stay in `sys_session`. Holds.

**(d) `redis-cache-adapter.ts` against the contract it states.**
- *TTL.* `set` writes `SET key value PX max(1, ceil(ttl × 1000))` when `ttl ?? defaultTtl` is positive, else a plain `SET`; `defaultTtl` defaults to `0` = no expiry. `MemoryCacheAdapter` expires at `now + ttl × 1000` for a positive effective TTL and never otherwise, with the same default, so the two agree, fractions included; the parity table pins both. Redis expires the key itself, so expiry is one event for every node; `has` is `EXISTS`, `delete` answers `DEL` count. The fixed-window counter re-sets the key with the remaining seconds (ceil), so the window end travels with the value and never slides. Holds.
- *Atomicity at the window boundary.* `ICacheService` has no atomic increment; `incrementFixedWindowOnce` and `consumeOnce` are GET then SET, serialised per key inside one process (`serializePerKey`) and not across processes. Two replicas counting one key in the same instant can both read `n` and both write `n + 1`, so a limit can over-admit by at most the number of concurrently counting replicas at the boundary, never multiply by N. That is the bounded imprecision ADR-0069 D2 accepts (its D2 row asks for a shared store, and `rate-limit-storage.ts` and `inbound-rate-limit.ts` already state this trade); the PR states it in the module header, the changeset, the README and the contract page. The two-process leg alternates requests one at a time on purpose, so it pins "one limit, not N" and not atomicity. Holds.
